title: The Document Skeleton 🦴
description: Learn the essential tags that every webpage needs: html, head, body.

slides.title: The Four Must‑Have Tags 🏷️
slides.content:
# Every Page Needs These

```html
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html>
  <head>
    ...
  </head>
  <body>
    ...
  </body>
</html>
```
- `<!DOCTYPE html>` tells the browser this is an HTML5 document.
- `<html>` wraps the entire page.
- `<head>` contains meta‑information (title, links to CSS, etc.).
- `<body>` holds all visible content.

slides.title: The <head> Section 🧠
slides.content:
# The Brain of the Page

The `<head>` is invisible to users but vital. It can contain:
- `<title>` – appears in the browser tab.
- `<meta>` tags – for character set, description, viewport.
- `<link>` – to attach CSS files.
- `<script>` – to load JavaScript (though best at the end of body).

Think of `<head>` as the page's ID card – it identifies and configures the page.

quizData.question: Which tag holds the content that users actually see?
quizData.explanation: The <body> element contains all visible content like headings, paragraphs, and images.

slides.title: The <body> Section 💪
slides.content:
# Where the Magic Happens

Everything you want visitors to see goes here:
- Text, images, links, videos.
- Navigation menus.
- Buttons and forms.

A common mistake for beginners is to put visible content inside `<head>` – it won't show up! Always place it in `<body>`.

slides.title: Pro Tip 🚀
slides.content:
## Always set the language

Adding `lang="en"` (or your language) to the `<html>` tag helps search engines and screen readers. It's a small detail with big accessibility benefits!

quizData.question: The <title> tag goes inside the <body> section.
quizData.explanation: The <title> belongs in the <head> because it's meta‑information, not visible page content.
